chapters.title: Fraction Equivalence and Comparison
chapters.key_rules: Compare fractions by reasoning about the size of the parts and how many parts there are: with the same denominator, more parts is greater; with the same numerator, smaller parts (bigger denominator) is less. Compare to benchmarks like 1/2 and 1, or rewrite with a common denominator. Equivalent fractions name the same point on the number line.

exercises.text: Which is greater: 1/8 or 1/10? Explain or show your reasoning.
Which is greater: 4/10 or 7/10? Explain or show your reasoning.
Which is greater: 4/5 or 5/4? Explain or show your reasoning.
Is 4/5 more or less than 1/2? Explain your reasoning.
Which fraction is greater: 2/5 or 2/6? Explain or show your reasoning.
Which fraction is greater: 5/8 or 7/8? Explain or show your reasoning.
Which fraction is greater: 9/10 or 103/100? Explain or show your reasoning.
There is a water fountain 7/10 mile from the start of a hiking trail. There is a pond 3/5 mile from the start. Walking from the start, which will a hiker come across first? Explain your reasoning.
List these fractions from least to greatest: 1/3, 5/12, 2/10. Explain or show your reasoning.
Name three fractions that are equivalent to 2/5. Explain or show your reasoning.
Explain why the fractions 10/3 and 40/12 are equivalent.
exercises.answer: Multiplying the numerator and denominator of 10/3 by 4 gives 40/12, so they name the same amount

exercises.text: Find a fraction that is between 2/5 and 3/8. Explain or show your reasoning.

chapters.title: Decimals with Tenths and Hundredths
chapters.key_rules: Tenths and hundredths can be written as fractions or decimals: 2/10 = 0.2 = 0.20 = 20/100. To compare decimals, compare place by place from the left: ones, then tenths, then hundredths. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

exercises.text: Compare 0.6 and 0.35. Which is greater? Explain your reasoning.
Which of these numbers are equivalent to 2/10: 0.5, 0.2, 20/100, 25/100, 0.20?
Order the numbers from least to greatest: 5.90, 9.05, 5.95, 0.59, 5.59.
Order the numbers from least to greatest: 13/10, 1.25, 1.46, 7/5, 155/100.

chapters.title: Comparing Positive and Negative Numbers
chapters.key_rules: On a number line, numbers increase to the right. A number to the left is less, even if its digits look bigger: -12 is greater than -15, and -12.5 is less than -12.

exercises.text: True or false: -5 > 2. Explain your reasoning.
True or false: 3 > -8. Explain your reasoning.
True or false: -12 > -15. Explain your reasoning.
True or false: -12.5 > -12. Explain your reasoning.
It is true that -8.7 < -8.4. Which number is further to the right on the number line?
Order these lowest points from least to greatest elevation: California -282 ft, Colorado 3350 ft, Louisiana -8 ft, New Mexico 2842 ft, Wyoming 3099 ft.
exercises.answer: California, Louisiana, New Mexico, Wyoming, Colorado
